articles.title: Tell HN: Don't mass spam employers with LLM generated emails
articles.title_ja: Tell HN: Don't mass spam employers with LLM generated emails
articles.summary_ja:
Title: Tell HN: Don't mass spam employers with LLM generated emails
HN text: If you're looking for a job, do -not- have Claude bulk email every company on "Who's Hiring". These things all look the same and your message is just going to get marked spam. For example, it's painfully obvious that our staff eng role's "combination of distributed execution, workload optimization, and cost-aware infrastructure" is not, in fact, "unusually close" to whatever line on your resume Claude decided is tangentially relevant. Just write a normal email by hand and send it. If you it looks like you spent 5 minutes looking up what we do and are actually excited I'll at least look at your resume; if you spent 0 minutes thinking about the job posting I'm going to spend 0 minutes on this too.

articles.title: Ask HN: Why not allow AI-written posts with a "human disclosure" section?
articles.title_ja: Ask HN: Why not allow AI-written posts with a "human disclosure" section?
articles.summary_ja:
Title: Ask HN: Why not allow AI-written posts with a "human disclosure" section?
HN text: Some research papers already have an "AI disclosure" section where the human authors indicate what they contributed and what the AI contributed to the paper. AI-written posts on social media could similarly have a "human disclosure" section where the AI indicates what the human user contributed and what the AI contributed to the post. Note that the content of the "human disclosure" section would be determined and written automatically by the AI based on its conversation with the human user. What do you think of this idea?
